title: Volume 4 · FIFO, Landed Cost and Valuation Reports
subtitle: Lessons 5–8: how FIFO layers produce cost of goods sold, how landed cost changes them, and the three reports a consultant is asked to defend
outcomes: Explain FIFO cost of goods sold from the layers rather than from the report
Use repost item valuation safely and know when it refuses to run
Read stock balance, stock ledger and stock ageing without confusing them
Decide whether negative stock should be blocked, and defend the answer

slides.title: Watch FIFO build layers, then consume the oldest
bullets: Each receipt creates a valuation layer at its own rate, and sales consume the oldest first
Cost of goods sold is the sum of the layers consumed, not a single average rate
Serial and batch numbers decide which units leave, but FIFO still fixes the cost
Changing valuation method after go-live is a migration, not a setting
slides.notes: The number to make the learner predict is one thousand four hundred sixty: ten units from the one twenty layer and two from the one thirty layer. If they say one thousand five hundred, they are averaging, which is a different valuation method. Show the two ledger rows rather than the report total, because the rows are the evidence and the report is only the summary.

slides.title: The cost arithmetic that must balance
bullets: Total value in equals total value out plus the value remaining, always
Averaging the two rates hides the layer structure and double-counts in mixed sales
Gross profit per line differs across the month even when the selling price does not
Reports that round to whole currency units must still reconcile to the stock ledger

rows: Cost of goods sold for 12 units
Value in equals value out plus remaining

slides.notes: Every valuation conversation ends with that identity: what came in equals what went out plus what is left. If it does not balance, a repost is pending, a landed cost arrived late, or someone posted a stock entry with a hand-typed rate. Make the learner write the identity on paper before opening any report, because it works for nine problems out of ten.

slides.title: Correct a wrong valuation with a repost, not a journal
bullets: Repost item valuation recalculates layers from history and rewrites downstream cost
It is the correct remedy when a rate was wrong, a landed cost arrived late or a period was opened wrongly
It refuses to run across a closed accounting period, which protects submitted reports
Every repost leaves a background job and a ledger movement, so run it deliberately

rows: Repost from 01-01-2026, based on valuation rate
Status Queued for the background worker
Posting date in the closed month

slides.notes: Reposts are the tool that keeps a migration honest, and they are also the tool that scares finance if used casually. Explain the trade: the recalculation is exact, but it changes cost of goods sold after the fact, so the month's profit moves. That is acceptable in the first two months of a go-live and unacceptable after the accounts are filed.

slides.title: Decide about negative stock before it decides for you
bullets: Allowing negative stock keeps operations moving but leaves valuation guessing
Blocking it forces the paperwork to catch up, which is usually what a controlled client wants
The setting lives in Stock Settings and applies to the whole company
Either way, the ageing report is the early warning that something is being issued twice

rows: Outgoing row with a warning rate
Bin returns to a positive balance

slides.notes: Most Malaysian distributors start with negative stock blocked, because a warehouse that cannot issue unrecorded goods learns to record receipts quickly. If a client insists on allowing it, agree a weekly negative stock report with a named owner, or the balance sheet will carry an unexplained valuation within one quarter. Either answer is defensible; silence is not.

slides.title: Balance, ledger and ageing in one pass
bullets: Three reports must agree before you present a stock number to anyone
Balance gives the number, ledger proves it, ageing raises the risk conversation
A repost changes the ledger and therefore the balance, so re-read both afterwards
Write the three figures on one page and keep it with the month-end pack

rows: Stock Ledger, last row for the item
unchanged if the original rate was right

slides.notes: The habit worth teaching is the one-page proof: three numbers, one source each, signed and dated. When a client questions stock value three weeks later, that page settles it without reopening the ledger. If the balance and the ledger disagree, a repost is still queued, and the answer is to wait rather than to explain.

slides.title: The three stock reports, and what each answers
bullets: Stock balance answers what is on hand and what it is worth today
Stock ledger answers why, one movement at a time, with the rate used
Stock ageing answers how long it has been sitting there and what it costs to keep
Reconciling the three to each other is a five minute monthly discipline

rows: What do we hold and what is it worth
Value includes items already sold but not delivered
Why did the quantity or value change
Rows are not in document order
Ageing is by receipt, not by last movement
Discounts change the selling side only

slides.notes: A consultant is asked about stock value more often than any other number, and the answer always starts with which report. Say stock balance for the number, stock ledger for the story, ageing for the risk. When the client's figure disagrees with the report, ask which of the three they are quoting, and the conversation halves in length.

slides.title: Valuation methods and when each is defensible
bullets: FIFO suits distribution where suppliers change rates between deliveries
Moving average suits steady buying where price swings are small and reporting simplicity matters
Standard cost only belongs where a costing team maintains the standard and variances are reviewed
The method must match the client's accounting policy, not the consultant's preference

rows: Layer creep makes old stock look cheap
Hides a bad purchase inside the average
Reports would need a manual restatement

slides.notes: Nine out of ten distribution clients should run FIFO, because their purchase rates genuinely move and their auditors expect the oldest stock to leave first. Say that plainly, but write it in the configuration worksheet with the client's signature, because the choice fixes how every margin report reads for the life of the system.

lab.title: Lab · Build FIFO layers, compute cost of goods sold and repair a valuation
steps: Receive 10 units of SM-BL200 at 120.00 and confirm layer one
Receive 10 more at 130.00 and confirm the bin value of 2,500.00
Sell 12 units and read the outgoing stock ledger row
Confirm cost of goods sold of 1,460.00 and remaining stock of 1,040.00
Prove the identity: value in equals value out plus value remaining
Post a repost item valuation for the item and read the resulting adjustment rows
Attempt a repost into a closed period and record the validation message
Block negative stock, attempt to oversell and record the error
lab.done: Done when cost of goods sold of 1,460.00 and remaining stock of 1,040.00 add to the 2,500.00 received, and both the repost and the negative-stock rules have been demonstrated.

quiz.question: Two receipts of 10 units at 120.00 and 10 at 130.00, then a sale of 12 units. FIFO cost of goods sold is what?
quiz.why: FIFO consumes the oldest layer first: 10 × 120 = 1,200 plus 2 × 130 = 260, giving 1,460.00.

quiz.question: Which identity must always hold after any stock movement?
options: Value in equals value out minus remaining
Value in equals value out plus value remaining
Value out equals value in plus remaining
Remaining equals value in plus value out
quiz.why: What was received must equal what was issued plus what remains. A break in that identity means a pending repost or a hand-typed rate.

quiz.question: When is repost item valuation the right tool?
options: To recalculate cost after a wrong rate or late landed cost
quiz.why: Repost recalculates valuation layers from history, which is exactly what a wrong rate or a late landed cost voucher requires.

quiz.question: What happens when you try to post a repost into a closed accounting period?
options: It posts to the next open period
quiz.why: ERPNext blocks valuation changes inside a closed period so that submitted financial statements cannot shift underneath the client.

quiz.question: Which report answers why a stock value changed?
quiz.why: The stock ledger holds every movement with its rate and voucher, so it explains the change rather than just stating the balance.

narration: Valuation is where a consultant earns trust, because the owner will check the margin with a calculator. Under FIFO, each receipt creates a layer, and a sale consumes the oldest first. Ten blenders at one hundred twenty and ten at one hundred thirty gives twenty five hundred of stock. Sell twelve and cost of goods sold is one thousand four hundred sixty, leaving eight units worth one thousand forty. That identity, value in equals value out plus value remaining, is the test for every valuation problem. When a rate was wrong or freight arrived late, the answer is a repost item valuation, not a journal entry, and the system will refuse to run it inside a closed period. And negative stock is a decision, not an accident: block it and operations learns to paperwork faster. Decide it, write it down, and the reports stop arguing. Every valuation question ends the same way: show the identity, then show the rows that prove it.
